To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
schistosomal infection in mice induces a SEA‐specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell response.
the immunization of mice by SEA induces an antigen‐specific CD8 T‐lymphocyte response, and this response may be of importance for the control of S. mansoni infection.
a single i.p immunization with schistosomal egg antigens (SEA) resulted in the in vitro induction of significant cytolytic T lymphocyte (CTl) activity in the splen of mice within 20 day.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel vaccine against schistosomiasis.
a better understanding of the mechanisms of protection induced by immunization with SEA.
the characterization of SEA‐specific CD 8 T cells and the demonstration of the relevance of these cells in the immune response against S. mansoni.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SEA‐specific CTL activity is a relevant component of the host immune response against S. mansoni infection.
SEA is able to induce a specific CD8+ T cell population with cytotoxic potential in mice, and that this population is involved in the protection against schistosomiasis.
SEA‐specific cytotoxic CD8 cells play a crucial role in the control of schistosomal granuloma formation and fibrosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SEA immunization induces a type 1 CD8+ T cell response which is able to protect mice from S. mansoni infection.
a SEA‐specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell population with cytotoxic potentiality is induced by immunization with SEA, and that these cells are involved in a type 1 immune response to SEA.
SEA‐specific CTL are induced in the course of S. mansoni infection and that their presence in the liver is related to the control of granuloma formation and fibrosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SEA can stimulate the generation of SEA‐specific CTL activity and that this activity could be of relevance for the control of schistosome infection.
SEA‐specific CTL activity is a major feature of S. mansoni infection.
the SEA‐induced CTL activity is able to reduce the number of granulo‐mas in the liver, and therefore the fibrotic response to the parasite.
